g.text: OKL — the Org Knowledge Layer (the 6th surface)
A lesson learned once protects every repo: source canons → curated seed files → one typed store → interest-filtered briefings before any task
Each repo's method surfaces, mined + curated
CLAUDE.md canon (330 lines) · frontend React canon
…plus every future repo that runs `okl record`
Scope + tags are the human curation step
+ geo enforcement · eval · deep-time lessons (3 newer files)
OKL STORE — one shared, typed body
SQLite file → shared service (Postgres) · one env var
SCOPE — who may see it (curation boundary)
org → propagates to every connected repo
repo:<name> → never leaks into another repo's check
RETRIEVAL — flat until a measured symptom
by decision (ADR: triggers at ~1k nodes / >10% miss rate)
THE LOOP — read before work, write after
scope filter → interest filter (tags) → BM25 rank
→ briefing leads with actions: FIX / ARM / AVOID
Symptom → Cause → Fix · scope + tags chosen by a human
UserPromptSubmit hook: briefing INTO context (blocks if unreachable)
Stop hook: "what did we learn?" (the write-side catch)
humans in the terminal · CI: okl drift --gate · okl metric
75% → 8% where baseline failed · React gap: 0% after seed
misses were coverage gaps → check doubles as detector
the origin repo's two-readers-one-canon decision record
WHY A 6TH SURFACE — "two readers, one canon" was really N readers, N canons
The five in-repo surfaces (canon · PR rules · architecture review · procedures · deep context) stay per-repo and unchanged. The OKL holds only the cross-repo subset —
org-scoped world-facts — enforced fail-closed at task time, the way the mechanical gates enforce at merge time. Repo quirks stay repo-scoped and never leak.
VERIFICATION — don't let a step grade itself
the grader is usually `ls`, not an LLM · verify at decision boundaries, not every micro-step · a step saying "done" and the work being done are different facts
"trust me" — a verified flag with no evidence.
runs the check, reads the REAL outcome, requires
the positive signal (exit 0 can't self-certify), stores
okl drift --gate + gates/run-gates.sh on every PR —
a mechanical grader with no stake in the claim.
VERIFIED_ON receipts written by the job that
watched a gate prove itself against real drift.
drift re-grades when governed files change after
verified_at · TTL decays unre-earned stamps to
the number the system can't flatter itself on.
